findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the detector avoids flagging its OWN test/gotcha fixtures (e.g. scope-exclude the detector's test module, an allowlist file with reviewed pins, or fragment-constructed patterns as check_criteria_vocabulary.py does) so the 'zero suppressions / tree scans clean' AC is achievable.
evidence: Plan: 'block-level scan (comment blocks + AST docstrings)' over 'src/ + tests/'
AC: 'passes the current remediated tree with zero suppressions'
Testing: 'the acceptor-arm gotchas (bug surfaced, ticket dirs must NOT accept ...)' — these gotcha strings must live in the test corpus, which is under the scanned tree
scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:19 'Build this expression from fragments so this checker does not exempt its own source' plus its allowlist file + EXCLUDED_PREFIXES/EXCLUDED_FILES
scripts/check_config_reads.py:20-27 scopes DEFAULT_ROOT to src/rebar and maintains a _PLUMBING exclusion set — the established pattern for a text guard avoiding self-match
ABSENCE: plan names no fixture-file exclusion, allowlist, or fragment-construction strategy for its own RED/gotcha corpus
findings.finding: The detector scans tests/ tree-wide and the plan mandates 'zero suppressions' + 'post-remediation tree scans clean', but the guard's own unit-test corpus must contain the exact rot-prone tokens it detects (dead SHAs like cf93b2b7ad, run/thread ids, 'bug surfaced', date+incident-verb strings) as RED and gotcha fixtures — the plan specifies no self-exclusion mechanism, so the guard would flag its own test fixtures and cannot be green with zero suppressions.
findings.location: Approach (2) CI guard; Testing; AC line 'CI guard fails on reintroduced rot-prone refs, passes the current remediated tree with zero suppressions'
scenarios: Detector unit tests place a dead SHA / run-id / 'bug surfaced' fixture in a scanned file (docstring or comment) and the CI guard's own tree scan then RED-flags that fixture
A gotcha compliant-example block ('ticket dirs') authored to prove non-triggering lands in a scanned file and is itself reported
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt a sibling-guard self-exclusion: either exclude the detector's own test module path from the scan (as check_config_reads.py scopes to src/rebar), OR ship a reviewed allowlist file with per-file count pins plus EXCLUDED_FILES (as check_criteria_vocabulary.py does), and state explicitly that the detector's fixtures live there — then reconcile the 'zero suppressions' wording to mean 'zero suppressions in remediation-scope source', not the fixture corpus.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the 'etc' denylist with an explicit, closed denylist (and/or make it a named, editable constant) so the exempt-hex set is a decision, not an executor guess.
evidence: 'SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters (denylist ed25519/sha256 etc)'
findings.finding: The SHA-like-hex denylist is left open-ended ('denylist ed25519/sha256 etc') — 'etc' defers completing the denylist to the executor, so which non-SHA hex/ident tokens are exempt is undecided.
scenarios: A legitimate token like 'b3sum', 'crc32', or a 7+ hex color/constant trips the detector because it wasn't on the guessed denylist
Post-remediation tree scan is not actually clean under the executor's denylist choices
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the full initial denylist (ed25519, sha256, sha512, blake2b, crc32, …) as a named constant in scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py and cover an FP gotcha for at least one denylisted token in the unit tests.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name check_config_reads.py (AST scan + '# read-via:' inline escape marker) and check_criteria_vocabulary.py (source scanner + allowlist) as prior art for the detector's scan mechanics and escape hatch, and state whether the new guard reuses their file-walk/exclusion/AST scaffolding and escape-marker idiom or consciously diverges (and why).
evidence: Plan: 'CI guard (detector is NET-NEW per Context; prior art/reuse: it follows the repo's scripts/check_*.py guard convention — check()/main() shape, wired as a named step ... like check_verify_gate_parity.py)' — cites the convention but no scan/escape-hatch analogue.

scripts/check_config_reads.py:1-9,23-24: AST-level check over src/rebar with a '# read-via: <pointer>' inline escape MARKER and the documented check()/main() API contract — the same detector+escape-hatch shape the plan proposes, unnamed.

scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:1-2,16-38: a repo-wide text-pattern source scanner that confines a deprecated pattern to reviewed records via an allowlist file, with directory-exclusion scaffolding — a near-sibling to the proposed block scanner, unnamed.
ANTI-FP: well-trodden in-repo lint pattern; no external prior-art search needed and no fully-novel architecture is introduced — finding scoped to in-repo reuse / anti-repackaging (Rule-of-Three).
findings.finding: The detector's scan/parse mechanics and the 'context: external' escape hatch are declared NET-NEW/novel without engaging two directly-analogous in-repo guards whose scaffolding they would reinvent: check_config_reads.py (AST scan over source + a '# read-via:' inline escape MARKER) and check_criteria_vocabulary.py (repo-wide pattern scanner + allowlist file). The plan names the generic check_*.py convention and the workflow wiring, but not these two escape-hatch/scan idioms the detector should reuse or consciously reject.
findings.location: Approach step (2) ('detector is NET-NEW per Context; prior art/reuse: it follows the repo's scripts/check_*.py guard convention'); escape hatch clause ('escape hatch "context: external"')
scenarios: Implementer builds a bespoke file-walk + directory-exclusion + AST-docstring harness and a fresh escape-hatch mechanism, diverging from the two existing scan/escape-marker idioms and increasing maintenance surface.
Reviewers of the guard PR cannot tell whether '#context: external' was chosen over the existing '# read-via:' inline-marker idiom deliberately or by oversight.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step (2), after the check_*.py convention citation, add: 'Scan/escape-hatch prior art: check_config_reads.py (AST docstring scan over source + `# read-via:` inline escape marker) and check_criteria_vocabulary.py (source-tree pattern scanner with directory exclusions + allowlist). Reuse their file-walk/exclusion scaffolding; model `#context: external` on the `# read-via:` inline-marker idiom rather than inventing a new escape mechanism.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the exact keyword tokens (and case rule) that arm the '>=8 digits' run/job/thread-id trigger, the way the verb set is enumerated.
evidence: 'run/job/thread id >=8 digits after keyword'
contrast: verb trigger is explicit — 'a past-tense incident verb from the ENUMERATED set {failed, broke, ...}'
findings.finding: The 'run/job/thread id' trigger is defined as '>=8 digits after keyword' but the keyword set is never enumerated, unlike the deliberately ENUMERATED past-tense verb set used for the date+verb trigger. The executor must guess which keyword tokens gate the id-length rule (run? job? thread? all three? case sensitivity?).
scenarios: A run id preceded by a non-listed synonym (e.g. 'build 30721408463') slips past the detector
Executor picks a different keyword set than the author intended, changing the census
findings.suggested_fix: State the keyword set explicitly, e.g. keyword ∈ {run, job, thread, build} (case-insensitive) within the same comment block, and give one triggering + one non-triggering example.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the detector's testable entrypoint (a pure function over comment-block/docstring TEXT, callable with literal strings) so the FP/acceptor unit tests exercise the real matching logic without requiring the fixtures to be scanned-in-place docstrings.
evidence: Plan defines the scan as 'comment blocks + AST docstrings'
Repo fixtures for guards are passed as literals to check()/module functions (tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads.py builds inputs programmatically), not as docstrings
ABSENCE: the plan does not state whether unit-test fixtures are exercised via the block/docstring parser or via a lower-level string entrypoint
findings.finding: The scan surface is defined as 'comment blocks + AST docstrings', but the RED/gotcha fixtures the Testing section depends on are typically string-literal arguments inside test-function bodies (not module/function docstrings), so the detector may not actually reach the strings its own unit tests feed it — leaving the trigger/acceptor arms untested against realistic fixture placement.
findings.location: Approach (2) 'block-level scan (comment blocks + AST docstrings)'; Testing
scenarios: A unit test passes 'bug surfaced' or a dead SHA as a Python string argument to the detector; if the detector only walks comment blocks + ast docstrings of a file, the fixture is either never scanned (test vacuously green) or must be a real docstring (re-entering the self-scan problem)

findings.finding: test_plan_review_explain.py is listed as a remediation site that should 'cite bug c7e3-dd16', but the file carries no rot-prone ref to remediate: its module docstring cites epics only by word-triple alias, with no SHA, run/thread id, or dated-incident narrative, and the plan supplies no line pin.
findings.location: Approach — site list, 'test_plan_review_explain.py cite bug c7e3-dd16'

findings.finding: The detector's 'date+evidence-verb' rot-prone rule names an 'evidence-verb' category with no enumerated verb set or matching rule, while the negative gotcha 'bug surfaced' must NOT accept — leaving the verb list and its interaction with the keyword-cite acceptor unspecified.

evidence: Approach: 'rot-prone = SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters (denylist ed25519/sha256 etc)'

Testing enumerates gotchas: "the acceptor-arm gotchas ('bug surfaced', 'ticket dirs' must NOT accept; grouped 4x4 ids and word-triple aliases MUST accept), escape hatch honored" — no denylist FP case named
AC4 covers 'bug surfaced'/'ticket dirs' and aliases/escape hatch but not the hex denylist
findings.finding: The detector defines a denylist (ed25519/sha256 etc.) to suppress SHA-like hex false positives, but the Testing section enumerates only the 'bug surfaced'/'ticket dirs' acceptor-arm gotchas and does not name a test that the denylisted tokens (e.g. an ed25519 key, sha256 literal) do NOT trigger the hex rule.
findings.location: Testing section / Approach (2) 'SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters (denylist ed25519/sha256 etc)'

'(17 pinned above as-of-plan: the original 15 census sites, of which 2 were later found under src/... plus 3 post-plan RUN-id sites minus overlap)'
'~15-17 pre-fix sites RED'
findings.finding: The remediation site count is narrated inconsistently across sections — Context says the ticket records '16 sites', Approach says '17 pinned above as-of-plan' with an arithmetic gloss ('15 census... plus 2 under src... plus 3 post-plan minus overlap') that a reader cannot obviously reconcile to 17, and Testing says '~15-17 pre-fix sites'.
